openings.claim: A manifest-ordered boundary ledger could distinguish the earliest witnessed divergence from an unresolved interval without treating timestamp order as execution order.
openings.delta: Change the ordering dependency from local timestamps to manifest stages and artifact boundaries. Carry paired digest comparisons and supporting record identifiers in a spreadsheet or script ledger. Mark missing records, missing digests and incomparable boundaries unknown. Inspect at most twelve records per pair and log each inspection; stop at sixty minutes. For every pair, retain a cited mismatch or an unresolved interval and a resource-feasible next check.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: a timestamp-first digest checklist with the same uncertainty rules and limits. The supplied export-before-parse timestamp should change checklist priority but leave manifest priority unchanged. Missing transform evidence should prevent both workflows from assigning that stage definitively. Removing a transform record should withdraw any claim depending solely on it, not imply nonexecution. Whether manifest ordering improves answer-sheet agreement is unknown.
openings.probe: Apply the two variants to the supplied disjoint three-pair subsets, including the final-review record removal. Freeze outputs before opening either sealed answer sheet. Within twenty additional minutes, compare supported boundaries, interval coverage and inspection counts. Subset differences confound an aggregate winner claim; audit individual incorrect claims against their references. A next check can inspect an available adjacent boundary record within the remaining allowance or verify digest comparability using the supplied dictionary; exhausted resources leave the interval unresolved.
assumptions: The manifest and dictionary permit corresponding artifact boundaries to be identified; otherwise comparisons remain unknown.
Available-record indexing fits the supplied environment. If time or inspection capacity runs out, unresolved intervals preserve the reporting obligation.

Defeat: manifest ordering or digest semantics cannot support the proposed alignment, or answer sheets expose unsupported narrowing. Equal boundary digests do not exclude an earlier transient divergence.

assessment: An exploratory review operation, not deployment or measured improvement. Blank warnings supply no success evidence. Definite stage claims require supplied record citations; causal explanations remain separate.
